introduction: The Indus Valley Civilization is one of the world’s earliest urban civilizations. It developed around 2500 BCE and is known for its advanced cities, trade, and culture. At this level, we will understand its basic facts in a simple way.

core_concepts.title: Time Period
core_concepts.description: The Indus Valley Civilization existed approximately from 2500 BCE to 1750 BCE. It is also called a Bronze Age civilization because copper and bronze were used.

core_concepts.title: Geographical Extent
core_concepts.description: This civilization spread across present-day Pakistan, western India, and parts of Afghanistan. It was mainly located around the Indus River and its tributaries.

core_concepts.title: Key Features
core_concepts.description: The main features include advanced urban planning, trade activities, seals, and a writing system that has not yet been deciphered.

core_concepts.title: Economy
core_concepts.description: It was primarily an agrarian economy where crops like wheat and barley were grown, along with active trade, especially with Mesopotamia.

core_concepts.title: Religion and Culture
core_concepts.description: People worshipped nature and animals. Evidence of Mother Goddess and Pashupati Mahadev figures has been found.

important_entities.name: Harappa
important_entities.significance: First site discovered by Daya Ram Sahni

important_entities.name: Mohenjo-daro
important_entities.significance: Discovered by Rakhal Das Banerjee, most developed city

important_entities.name: Lothal
important_entities.significance: Famous for its dockyard and trade center

important_entities.name: Kalibangan
important_entities.significance: Evidence of ploughed field found here

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Students often assume that the Indus script has been decoded, but it remains undeciphered to this day.
This was a Bronze Age civilization, so iron was not used.
Very few remains of horses have been found, so it is incorrect to consider it a horse-based civilization.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Remember 25 to 17, catch the Indus trend
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Helps recall the period from 2500 BCE to 1750 BCE easily.
Harappa was the first discovered site, and Mohenjo-daro was the most developed city.
Urban planning, trade, and undeciphered script are key identifiers of the Indus Civilization.

exam_strategy_tips: If a question mentions 'undeciphered script', immediately associate it with the Indus Civilization.
Questions related to time period and major sites are often direct, so use tricks instead of rote memorization.
